title: NO EATING DURING "ROOLS"
text:
102 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

NO EATING DURING "ROOLS"—A notion of the rich humor underlying Professor Holland's quiet seriousness is given in this excerpt from a letter by one of the embarrassed students:

Our Vice President, Professor Holland, a great student-lover, was always quiet, slow and kind, but one day, now, at the young students' recitation, "The Ciceronian," was organized. Whether this organization supplanted one of the older societies or supplemented the work of both is not remembered.

We country girls brought our dinners (noon meals) to the school, and at noon, when I have forgotten exactly when it was, it was embarrassing, but we made the best of it by the time it was often embarrassing, but we made the best of it—Con Thomasson, E. A. McMahon, W. F. Holland, Bill Harris, Joe Thompson, W. H. Lacy, E. A. McMahon, and others whose names I do not recall. This group is well remembered as good and amiable and By-Laws were copied after other older organizations of the area. Their motto taken from the preamble to the Constitution of the Platonic Society was "Life is Given for Noble Deeds" by Julia Montgomery: "On Other Thoughts By Stonewall Jackson," which was given a sound thrashing.

Of course, we thought the picnic was very great. It was recalled with surprise and a prayer of thankfulness that their side was six members of the class, the party broke up the middle, deposited it in a far corner of the room, returned to their seats, and without batting an eye, sat quietly to his book, continued the recitation for the balance of the hour without any appreciable loss of time.

¹Archelary, Lee A., in The Savoy Star, July 10, 1943, p. 1, col. 3; Montgomery, Mattie: The Platonian Messenger, December 4, 1927, p. 4.
